title: CBDT's New Crypto Reporting Guidance: What Investors Need to Know
description: The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) has issued guidance aligning India's crypto reporting with global OECD standards. This framework focuses on how crypt.

faq.q: Does this guidance introduce new taxes on crypto assets?
faq.a: No, this guidance does not introduce any new taxes on crypto assets. It operationalises the reporting framework, meaning it clarifies *how* information about existing taxable transactions will be collected and shared.

faq.q: Who is responsible for reporting under this new guidance?
faq.a: Crypto-Asset Service Providers (CASPs) like exchanges and brokers are responsible for collecting transaction data from users and reporting it to the tax authorities, not individual investors directly.

faq.q: How does this affect NRIs investing in crypto?
faq.a: NRIs should be aware that their crypto transactions, whether through Indian or international platforms, may now be subject to information exchange between tax authorities globally, impacting their tax compliance in both India and their country of residence.

faq.q: What kind of records should I keep for my crypto investments?
faq.a: You should keep detailed records of every transaction, including the date, type of crypto asset, quantity, value in INR at the time of transaction, purchase/sale price, and any associated fees.

faq.q: What if I use a decentralised exchange (DEX) or a foreign exchange?
faq.a: While the immediate reporting obligation falls on regulated CASPs, the spirit of the guidance is global transparency. Using DEXs or foreign exchanges does not exempt you from your personal tax liabilities in India, and meticulous record-keeping remains paramount.

faq.q: Can losses from crypto be offset against other income?
faq.a: No, under current Indian tax laws for Virtual Digital Assets (VDAs), losses from crypto assets cannot be set off against gains from other crypto assets, nor against any other income.

faq.q: Will this guidance lead to more scrutiny from the tax department?
faq.a: Yes, by providing tax authorities with more structured and comprehensive data on crypto transactions, it is likely to increase scrutiny and improve compliance, ensuring investors accurately declare their crypto income.
